findings.finding: The admission guard is placed in gate_source.py / repo_snapshot.py, but the incident's ENOSPC clone that produced VOTER_ERROR / coverage-gap (review-error) is gc.clone_change_ref(...) into tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='reviewbot-') in voter.py, a separate step from the attested-snapshot materialize() path those two files own.
findings.location: Part B — near-full review admission control; File impact (gate_source.py / repo_snapshot.py)
scenarios: A guard added only ahead of materialize() lets clone_change_ref proceed and ENOSPC exactly as in the incident, re-producing the fail-closed -1 the plan exists to prevent

findings.checklist_item: Specify that the near-full admission check measures free space of the volume the review clone actually writes to (the clone/temp target), not unconditionally the snapshot-store volume the janitor computation defaults to.
evidence: janitor _gc_pass: `usage = shutil.disk_usage(str(root))` where root = store_root() = $REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR/rebar-gate-snapshots
voter.py:624 clones into `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory` which resolves to tempfile.gettempdir()
REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR is an operator override that can point the store at a different (roomier) volume than gettempdir (repo_snapshot.store_root docstring: 'operators point it at a roomy local FS')
findings.finding: The plan reuses the janitor's free-space computation, but that computation measures the snapshot-store volume (shutil.disk_usage on repo_snapshot.store_root = $REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR/rebar-gate-snapshots), while the review clone that ENOSPCs writes to tempfile.gettempdir(); the plan does not pin which volume the admission floor must measure.
findings.location: Part B — 'check volume-relative free space using the existing snapshot janitor free-space computation'; File impact (janitor.py reuse/export)
scenarios: Operator sets REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR to a large data volume; the janitor free-space check reads that volume as healthy while the root volume (where the clone lands) is full — admission control passes and the clone still ENOSPCs
findings.suggested_fix: Have the reused/exported free-space helper take the target path (the clone temp dir) and run shutil.disk_usage against THAT path, so it measures the volume that can ENOSPC.

findings.checklist_item: Reconcile AC1's 'below the soft threshold' guarantee with the fact that the escalated reclaim only frees the build cache — either scope AC1 to 'frees the full reclaimable build cache (bytes_freed>0)' rather than an absolute post-threshold, or extend the acute tier to also reclaim the other measured consumers (dangling/exited containers, snapshot store) so the threshold guarantee is real.
evidence: Evidence: 'Build Cache: 111 entries, 5.244 GB, 100% reclaimable'; 'Images: 4, all ACTIVE ... only 144 MB reclaimable'; 'Containers: 3.572 GB; Local Volumes: 947 MB; snapshot store: 1.4 GB'
Part A: escalate to `docker builder prune -f` with keep→0 — touches only the buildkit cache; images are ACTIVE and prune_docker_caches' `docker image prune -f` only drops dangling
AC1: reclaim 'returns disk use below the soft threshold'
findings.finding: AC1 requires the escalated reclaim to return disk use below the soft threshold, but Part A's escalation only drops the build cache (keep→0); the incident evidence shows the build cache was 5.244 GB of a 95%-used 30 GiB disk, with containers (3.572GB), images (2.802GB), volumes (947MB) and snapshot store (1.4GB) making up the rest — so freeing only the cache may not, in general, land below the soft threshold.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria bullet 1; Part A — acute-pressure emergency reclaim tier; Evidence (docker system df figures)
scenarios: Recovery in the real incident required a full reboot + manual prune to reach 74%; if non-cache consumers alone exceed the soft threshold, keep→0 on the cache cannot reach below it and AC1 is unsatisfiable on real disk (only assertable via the stub test)
